description: Explanations and career advice rather than fixing a blocker.

messages.text: Newbie question: why do we use a double-entry ledger instead of just storing balances?
messages.label: core

messages.text: Great question! Double-entry means every money movement is two rows that must sum to zero — so we can always prove balances are correct and audit any change. Balances are derived, never stored as truth. Happy to whiteboard it in our 1:1.
messages.label: mentoring

messages.text: How do you decide when to write an ADR vs just a PR description?
messages.label: core

messages.text: Rule of thumb: if someone in 6 months will ask 'why did we do it this way?', write an ADR. PR descriptions explain the change; ADRs explain the decision and alternatives.
messages.label: mentoring

messages.text: How should I approach my first on-call shift? A bit nervous.
messages.label: core

messages.text: Totally normal! Shadow me for the first shift. Read the top 5 runbooks, know how to page for help, and remember: mitigate first, root-cause later. You won't be alone.
messages.label: mentoring

messages.text: What's a good way to structure the fraud rules design doc so reviewers don't get lost?
messages.label: core

messages.text: Lead with the decision you need, then constraints, then options with trade-offs in a table. Put the rule DSL details in an appendix. Reviewers mostly need page 1.
messages.label: mentoring

messages.text: What's the difference between our risk score and the fraud rules?
messages.label: core

messages.text: Risk score is a model output (probability); rules are deterministic policies on top of it. Rules can block, the score alone never does.
messages.label: mentoring

messages.text: How do you usually frame design trade-offs for the eng team?
messages.label: core

messages.text: Show the user impact first, then effort. Engineers respond well to 'this saves 2 taps for 60% of users' plus a rough cost estimate.
messages.label: mentoring

messages.text: Any tips for synthesising 12 interviews quickly?
messages.label: core

messages.text: Affinity map on a whiteboard, cluster by job-to-be-done, then pick the 3 strongest themes with quotes. Don't try to cover everything.
messages.label: mentoring

messages.text: How do I get better at estimating tasks? I keep underestimating.
messages.label: core

messages.text: Break it down until each piece is under a day, then add a buffer for unknowns — usually 30%. Track estimate vs actual for a month, you'll calibrate fast.
messages.label: mentoring

messages.text: How should I communicate the Billing v2 launch risk to leadership?
messages.label: core

messages.text: One slide: what could go wrong, likelihood, blast radius, and the rollback plan. Leadership cares most about the rollback.
messages.label: mentoring
